# WebScheduler — Marketing Site & Developer Portal

The public-facing static site, deployed to the marketing domain (e.g. root of
`webscheduler.co.za`). Completely separate from the CI4 application (which lives at the
app subdomain). It ships the marketing pages **and** the developer API portal at
`/developer`.

---

## 1. Hard rule: NOT part of the app build (Owner Section)

The marketing site is committed to the repo but must **never** be bundled into the
WebScheduler application build or deployment package. This is enforced structurally —
do not break it:

- **Vite** (`npm run build`): `vite.config.js` inputs list specific `resources/js` /
  `resources/scss` files only. Never add a `marketing-site/` entry point.
- **App Tailwind** (`tailwind.config.js`): `content` scans `app/Views`, `resources/`,
  `public/`. Do NOT add `marketing-site/` to it — the site has its own
  `marketing-site/tailwind.config.cjs`.
- **Deployment package** (`scripts/package.js`): copies an explicit `essentialFiles`
  allowlist (`app`, `public`, `vendor`, `writable`, `spark`, …). `marketing-site/` is
  not in it and must not be added.

If you need to verify: `marketing-site/` should never appear in `public/build/`,
`webschedulr-deploy/`, or any release ZIP.

---

## 2. Layout

```
marketing-site/
  index.html features.html pricing.html about.html contact.html   # pages
  README.md
  src/styles.css              # Tailwind input (@font-face Inter + @tailwind + components)
  tailwind.config.cjs         # brand tokens (mirrors the app), scans marketing-site/**/*.html
  assets/
    logo.svg                  # WebScheduler brand mark, ocean #003049 (recolored from default)
    og-image.png              # 1200×630 social share card (generated, committed)
    site.js                   # theme toggle + mobile menu
    consent.js                # cookie consent banner (Consent Mode v2)
    styles.css                # GENERATED by `npm run site:css` — git-ignored
    fonts/inter-latin-{400,500,600,700,800}-normal.woff2   # self-hosted Inter
    screenshots/*.png         # real app screenshots (committed)
docs-site/                    # developer API portal templates (Redoc) — see §8
scripts/
  capture-screenshots.js      # Playwright screenshot capture
  build-marketing-site.js     # assembles dist/site/
  build-docs-site.js          # assembles the developer portal (reused by the above)
```

Build output → `dist/site/` (git-ignored). The whole `dist/site/` folder is the
deployable; upload its contents to the host root.

---

## 3. Commands

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `npm run site:shots` | Capture real app screenshots via Playwright → `marketing-site/assets/screenshots/` |
| `npm run site:css`   | Compile Tailwind once → `marketing-site/assets/styles.css` (for local source preview) |
| `npm run site:dev`   | Same, `--watch` for live editing |
| `npm run site:build` | Build the deployable site → `dist/site/` (minified CSS, bundled `/developer`, robots.txt, sitemap.xml) |

Local preview: `npm run site:dev` + `python3 -m http.server 8080 --directory marketing-site`.
**Serve over HTTP, never `file://`** — the Redoc portal fetches its spec over HTTP and
self-hosted fonts resolve relatively.

---

## 4. Build pipeline & guards (Owner Section)

`scripts/build-marketing-site.js` order (do not reorder without care):
1. Clean + recreate `dist/site/`.
2. Copy the 5 HTML pages.
3. Copy `assets/` **skipping `styles.css`** (see below).
4. **Compile Tailwind AFTER the asset copy** → `dist/site/assets/styles.css`. Compile
   must run after the copy so the minified build is authoritative and a locally
   generated `assets/styles.css` (from `site:css`) never clobbers it.
5. Bundle the developer portal (runs `build-docs-site.js`, copies into `dist/site/developer/`).
6. Guards (below).
7. Generate `robots.txt` + `sitemap.xml`.

Two build guards **fail the build** — respect them:

- **External-host guard.** Only `src=`/`href=` URLs on an allowlist are permitted:
  `webscheduler.co.za`, `www.googletagmanager.com`, `www.google-analytics.com`. Any
  other CDN/font/host reference fails. The site is otherwise fully self-contained
  (inline everything, self-host fonts). *(OG/canonical use `content=`/`href=` to our own
  domain, which is allowlisted.)*
- **Positioning guard.** Fails on `open source`, `open-source`, `free plan`,
  `free tier`, `free forever`, `100% free` in any page. See §5.

---

## 5. Positioning rules (non-negotiable)

The product is positioned as **self-hosted, paid, starting at R160/month**.

- **Never** use free / open-source / no-fee-because-free messaging. The self-hosted
  angle ("your infrastructure, your data, your brand") is a differentiator, not a
  free/OSS claim.
- Pricing: Starter **R160/month** is the stated offer. Professional (R420) and Business
  (R890) are editable placeholders. Currency is ZAR.
- The positioning guard in the build enforces the banned phrases.

---

## 6. Design alignment with the app

The site must read as one system with the product:

- Brand tokens mirror the app in `marketing-site/tailwind.config.cjs`: primary/ocean
  `#003049`, accent/orange `#F77F00`, golden `#FCBF49`, crimson `#D62828`, cream
  `#EAE2B7`, `shadow-brand*`. Owner of the app-side tokens is [[webscheduler-ui-ux]].
- Font: **Inter, self-hosted** via `@font-face` in `src/styles.css` (no Google Fonts
  link — that would fail the external-host guard).
- **Dark mode uses the same `localStorage['xs-theme']` contract as the app** (inline
  FOUC guard in each page `<head>`; `.dark` class on `<html>`; toggle in `site.js`).
  The app-side FOUC mechanism is owned by [[webscheduler-frontend]].
- Icons are inline SVG (no Material Symbols font — again, no external requests).
- Screenshots are shown in a `.browser-frame` chrome.

---

## 7. Screenshots (`scripts/capture-screenshots.js`)

Playwright captures the 7 real app screens (login, dashboard, user-management,
appointments, services, customers, analytics) at 1440×900 @2x, **light mode**.

Prerequisites (see [[webscheduler-operations]] / the `verify` skill for the local-run
recipe):
- App running at `BASE_URL` (default `http://localhost:8080`).
- Sample data seeded: `php spark db:seed SchedulingSampleDataSeeder` (password
  `SamplePass!23`).
- An **admin** login — the sample seeder only creates provider/staff. Create a
  throwaway admin (bcrypt `password_hash`, `xs_users` + `xs_user_roles`) and delete it
  after; pass creds via `ADMIN_EMAIL` / `ADMIN_PASSWORD` env vars.

The script forces `xs-theme=light` and strips the CI4 dev debug toolbar
(`[id*="debug"]`) before each shot. Re-run after any app UI change so marketing
screenshots stay current.

---

## 8. Developer portal (`docs-site/` → `/developer`)

The public API reference. **`scripts/build-docs-site.js` is the single source of truth**
for assembling it (also used standalone as `npm run docs:build` → `dist/developer/`).
`build-marketing-site.js` runs it and copies the output to `dist/site/developer/`.

- Templates: `docs-site/index.html` (Redoc reference) and `docs-site/getting-started.html`.
- Runtime: vendored `resources/redoc/redoc.standalone.js` (no CDN — its build guard
  fails if it references `cdn.redoc.ly`).
- Spec: `docs/technical/openapi.yml` → published as `openapi.yaml`. The API contract
  itself is owned by [[webscheduler-api-contract]]; the app also serves this spec at
  runtime via `DeveloperDocs` (see `scripts/package.js` which ships the yml).
- Redoc theme primary is brand ocean `#003049`; topbar links back to the marketing
  site (`../`).
- **Redoc requires HTTP** — opening `dist/site/developer/index.html` via `file://`
  shows "process is not defined" and a Redoc blob-URL request; both are harmless
  `file://` artifacts, not bugs.
- Linked from every marketing page (nav + footer "Developers") and a homepage
  "For developers" callout.

---

## 9. SEO

Per-page `<head>` contains: `<title>`, meta description, `rel=canonical`,
`robots`, Open Graph + Twitter card tags (image = `assets/og-image.png`, absolute URL),
`theme-color` (light/dark), and JSON-LD (`Organization` on all pages;
`SoftwareApplication` + Offer R160 on home & pricing).

- `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml` are **generated by the build** from `BASE_URL` +
  page list (6 URLs incl. `/developer/`), with today's `lastmod`.
- **`BASE_URL` is hardcoded to `https://webscheduler.co.za`** in
  `build-marketing-site.js` AND baked into each page's canonical/OG tags. If the domain
  changes, update both.
- Google Search Console verification tag is on `index.html` with a **placeholder
  token** — replace before relying on it.
- When adding/editing pages, keep canonical/OG/JSON-LD in sync and add the page to the
  sitemap list in the build script.

---

## 10. Analytics & cookie consent (POPIA/GDPR)

- **GA4 measurement ID: `G-J8R1WZ2RLX`** — inline gtag snippet in every page's `<head>`
  (marketing + both portal pages).
- **Google Consent Mode v2**: consent defaults to `denied` for all signals; the snippet
  re-applies a stored `granted` on load. GA loads but stores/collects nothing until the
  visitor accepts.
- **Consent banner**: `marketing-site/assets/consent.js` — self-injecting, styled for
  light/dark, Accept/Decline, remembers the choice in `localStorage['ws-consent']`,
  works on marketing pages and the portal (loaded via `../assets/consent.js` there).
- A footer **"Cookie preferences"** control (`[data-consent-open]`) reopens the banner
  so consent can be withdrawn.
- To change GA behavior to "do not load until accepted", gate the `gtag/js` script tag
  in `consent.js` instead of using default-denied.

---

## 11. Editing multiple pages

The 5 pages are standalone HTML that duplicate the header/footer/head. When changing a
shared element across all pages, prefer a small one-off Node codemod (idempotent, unique
anchors) over 5 manual edits — that's how the nav "Developers" link, GA, and SEO blocks
were applied. Delete the codemod after running it.

---

## 12. Deploy

```bash
npm run site:build      # → dist/site/
```
Upload the **contents of `dist/site/`** to the marketing host root. The developer portal
lands at `/developer`. `dist/` and `marketing-site/assets/styles.css` are git-ignored.
This deploy is independent of the app release (`npm run release:*`).
